title: Cleanup after the migration-source pin: delete the dead DEPLOY_MIGRATION_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH guard, fold the image build onto git-source-extract, fix the gated migrate-down-real sha
description:
SUCCESSOR of task-d85fd8fd74354e94886d619c67f24c75 (migrations run from the working tree, not the built sha), filed 2026-09-09 by architect-ed42e60a at that row's plan time. Depends on it. Cut out of the parent to hold its roster at 8 files; nothing here is load-bearing for the pin itself, but each item is a real lie or a real duplicate the parent leaves behind. A malformed copy (task-0a65c201, empty description) was deleted minutes before this one was filed.

(1) DELETE THE DEAD GUARD. deploy-migration-context.ts:129-135 refuses DEPLOY_MIGRATION_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH only when `request.workspace` is passed AND differs from the configured workspace — a PATH STRING compare — and NEITHER production caller passes it (deploy-command.ts:280, rollback-restore.ts:130-133). Its comment :129-131 claims it prevents "migrating a different tree than the one the deploy archived", which was never true and after the parent is simply the parent's job. Measured references, exactly three: the roster entry :47-48 (DEPLOY_MIGRATION_CONTEXT_DETAILS, 3 codes -> 2; DeployMigrationContextCode :53 narrows automatically), the `request.workspace` key :103-105, the guard :129-135; and in deploy-migration-context.test.ts arm (d) :168-172 first block, arm (e) :206-207 entry, and the helper's `named` param :89-92. NO control-room mirror (live-runs.ts:86 has no migration codes), NO tests/security roster, NO count assertion, NO PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS / SAFE_PHASES row (resolver refusals reach the ledger with detail ""). Do NOT revive it as an interim `git diff --quiet` guard: that would refuse every rollback that crosses a migration-adding sha (deploy-service.ts:356-363 re-executes at the OLD sha with no rollbackImage fence at :310), would refuse dump restores that never read migrations/ (rollback-restore.ts:143-146), and on a shared-checkout fleet any peer's dirt in migrations/ would block every deploy under a code whose prose names a config error.

(2) FOLD THE TWIN RECIPE. The parent lands apps/daemon/src/repository/git-source-extract.ts (bare temp repo + objects/info/alternates + `<sha>^{commit}` verify + checkout-from-bare + prefix-fenced teardown), lifted from deploy-image-build.ts:16,:29-38,:41-45. Make deploy-image-build.ts call the helper for its bare-repo half so the two do not drift; its four arms in deploy-image-build.test.ts (66 lines) stay green unedited, including :20 "despite dirty files".

(3) THE GATED TWIN'S SHA. apps/daemon/src/deployment/migrate-down-real.test.ts (205 lines, `RUN` :48, MOE_MIGRATION_RESTORE=1) materializes a non-git tree :66-83, writes ADDED into the working tree :168-170, then passes a constant `sha: SHA` :51/:173. After the parent, the real port extracts migrations/ at that sha from the workspace's repo — a non-repo with a fake sha refuses before the tool runs, so this gated arm goes RED the next time anyone runs it live. Fix: git init + commit each written migration and pass its real sha. The parent fixes the ungated twin (migration-real.test.ts:51-81) itself.

(4) OPTIONAL, decide at plan time: a distinct MIGRATION_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE code for "the sha or its migrations/ is not in this repository" instead of the parent's byte-parity mapping onto MIGRATION_FAILED/MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN. Costs three rosters (migration-receipt.ts:13-26 codeLayers, deploy-ledger.ts:39-53 PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS, deploy-refusal-redaction.test.ts:68-76 SAFE_PHASES + :227 count). Only worth it if an operator has actually been confused by the parity code; otherwise leave it.
definitionOfDone: DEPLOY_MIGRATION_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH no longer exists in the tree: git grep returns zero hits across apps packages tests docs, the roster shrinks 3 -> 2, and deploy-migration-context.test.ts arms (d) and (e) are rewritten to the two surviving codes with no arm made vacuous.

deploy-image-build.ts composes git-source-extract for its bare-repo half; `git grep -n 'objects/info/alternates' -- apps/daemon/src` hits only the helper; deploy-image-build.test.ts's four arms including :20 "despite dirty files" pass UNEDITED.
migrate-down-real.test.ts commits each migration it writes and passes the real sha; run once under MOE_MIGRATION_RESTORE=1 with docker up and quote the count line — an unrun gated arm is not a pass.
If a MIGRATION_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE code is added, all three rosters move together and the redaction count arm is updated; if not, the completion record says so in one sentence.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck and pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with count lines quoted; no control-room or security roster is touched (assert by git diff --stat).

implementationPlan.description:
RE-MEASURE AGAINST THE LANDED PARENT. NO EDITS.

This row is gated on task-d85fd8fd. When you start, that row is DONE — but everything I measured while planning came from its UNCOMMITTED working tree, so confirm it against the landed commit before building on it.

CONFIRM THE HELPER'S ACTUAL SURFACE at apps/daemon/src/repository/git-source-extract.ts. As I measured it:
  `export async function extractCommittedPath(git: GitRunner, request: CommittedSourceRequest): Promise<CommittedSourceResult>`
  `CommittedSourceRequest = { destination, path, repository, sha }`, destination caller-owned ("The caller creates and removes it")
  `CommittedSourceResult = "OK" | "SOURCE_COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE" | "SOURCE_PATH_UNAVAILABLE"`
If the name, the request shape or the union moved during the parent's steps 7-8, the plan below still holds but the call sites change; say so rather than adapting silently.

RE-CENSUS ITEM 1, BECAUSE THE FILED ROSTER IS STALE. `git grep -n DEPLOY_MIGRATION_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH` over apps, packages, tests and docs returned exactly THREE hits when I measured: deploy-migration-context.ts:47 (roster entry), :134 (the guard — filed as :129-135, already shifted), and deploy-migration-context.test.ts:171 (filed as :168-172). The description's other three references — the `request.workspace` key, arm (e)'s entry, the helper's `named` param — do NOT carry the literal and must be found by READING both files. Confirm the description's claims that there is no control-room mirror, no security roster entry and no count assertion; the parent has been editing neighbours, so verify rather than trust.

UNDERSTAND WHY DoD 2's GREP LOOKS ALREADY-SATISFIED. `git grep -n 'objects/info/alternates' -- apps/daemon/src` returns NOTHING today because git grep skips untracked files and the helper is `??`. deploy-image-build.ts:41 has the write. Once the parent lands, the grep hits BOTH files, and DoD 2's gate is that it then hits only the helper.

ITEM 1 — DELETE THE DEAD GUARD (deploy-migration-context.ts and its test) (DoD 1).

Remove all six references, and delete the FIELD as well as the check:
- the `DEPLOY_MIGRATION_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH` entry in `DEPLOY_MIGRATION_CONTEXT_DETAILS` (3 codes -> 2; `DeployMigrationContextCode` narrows automatically since it is derived from the roster);
- the `request.workspace` KEY on the request shape;
- the guard itself and its comment.
Leaving an optional field nothing reads is how a dead guard grows back with a new justification.

IN THE TEST: rewrite arm (d) and arm (e) to the two SURVIVING codes, and update the helper's `named` parameter. DoD 1 says no arm may be made vacuous — an arm that previously proved a refusal must now prove a different, real refusal, not merely stop asserting. If an arm has no remaining subject, delete it and say so rather than leaving a shell that asserts nothing.

WHY THE GUARD GOES, so nobody restores it: it fires only when `request.workspace` is passed AND differs from the configured workspace, a PATH STRING compare, and NEITHER production caller passes it (deploy-command.ts:280, rollback-restore.ts:130-133). Its comment claims it prevents "migrating a different tree than the one the deploy archived", which was never what a path compare could prove, and after the parent's pin it is the parent's job.

DO NOT REVIVE IT AS AN INTERIM `git diff --quiet` CHECK. It would refuse every rollback crossing a migration-adding sha (deploy-service.ts:356-363 re-executes at the OLD sha), refuse dump restores that never read migrations/ (rollback-restore.ts:143-146), and on this shared-checkout fleet any peer's dirt in migrations/ would block every deploy under a code whose prose names a config error.

ITEM 2 — SHARE THE BARE-REPO RECIPE, AND IT IS NOT A DIRECT CALL (DoD 2). Read this before writing.

`createDeploymentImageBuilder` CANNOT simply call `extractCommittedPath`. The helper removes its temporary bare repo in a `finally` before returning, while the builder must hand that directory to `archiveIntoDocker` and needs it ALIVE until docker has consumed it. Wiring the call directly typechecks green and builds against a deleted directory.

EXTRACT THE SHARED PRIMITIVE INSTEAD. Exactly this much is duplicated, and it is worth sharing: verify `<sha>^{commit}` via rev-parse; resolve `--git-path objects` to an absolute path and reject CR/LF/NUL in it; `mkdtempSync` under `tmpdir()`; `git init --bare --template= --object-format=<sha1|sha256>`; write `objects/info/alternates`. Give it a shape whose CALLER owns teardown — either return the directory and let the caller run the prefix-fenced `rmSync`, or take a callback and tear down around it. Then `extractCommittedPath` composes it and adds its `--show-toplevel` check plus the checkout; the builder composes it and adds the docker archive.

DECIDE THE `core.autocrlf=false` QUESTION DELIBERATELY. The helper's `GIT` array carries it and the builder's does not. Whichever way the shared primitive goes, that flag starts applying to a path it did not before or stops applying to one it did. The helper's own comment explains why IT carries the flag; say in the completion record whether that reasoning transfers to an image archive, and which behaviour you chose.

THE FOUR ARMS IN deploy-image-build.test.ts MUST PASS UNEDITED, including :20 "despite dirty files". That file is NOT an owned path. If a change makes an arm fail, the fold changed the builder's behaviour — fix the fold, do not touch the arm.

DoD 2's GATE: after this, `git grep -n 'objects/info/alternates' -- apps/daemon/src` hits ONLY the shared primitive's file.

ITEM 3 — GIVE THE GATED TWIN A REAL SHA (migrate-down-real.test.ts) (DoD 3).

The arm materializes a NON-GIT tree at :66-83, writes its ADDED migration into the working tree at :168-170, and passes a constant `sha: SHA` at :51 and :173. After the parent's pin the real port extracts `migrations/` at that sha FROM THE WORKSPACE'S REPOSITORY — so a non-repo with a fabricated sha refuses before the migration tool ever runs, and this arm reds the next time anyone runs it live. It is gated on `RUN` (:48, `MOE_MIGRATION_RESTORE=1`), which is why nobody has seen it yet.

FIX: `git init` the materialized tree, COMMIT each migration as it is written, and pass the resulting real sha. The arm's subject is the down-migration behaviour, not git — so keep the git work minimal and obvious, and make sure the sha passed to the port is the one that actually contains the migration under test, not merely the latest commit.

The parent fixes the UNGATED twin (migration-real.test.ts:51-81) itself; do not touch it here.

DoD 3 REQUIRES YOU TO RUN IT: docker up, `MOE_MIGRATION_RESTORE=1`, and quote the count line. An unrun gated arm is NOT a pass and the DoD says so. If docker is unavailable to you, say that plainly in the completion record rather than quoting a skip as evidence — a skipped gated arm is the exact shape this row exists to stop shipping.

ITEM 4, THE GATES, AND THE ADVERSARIAL PASS (DoD 4, DoD 5).

ITEM 4 IS DECIDED: DO NOT ADD `MIGRATION_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`. The row asks the planner to decide and the answer is no. Its own test is "only worth it if an operator has actually been confused by the parity code", and no such confusion is recorded on this board; it costs three rosters plus a redaction count assertion, and one of those rosters is contentious under a concurrent row. The helper already distinguishes `SOURCE_COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE` from `SOURCE_PATH_UNAVAILABLE` internally, so the information exists where a debugger can reach it. DISCHARGE DoD 4 WITH ONE SENTENCE in the completion record saying it was considered and declined, and why — the clause asks for exactly that.

GATES (DoD 5): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, both EXIT 0, both count lines quoted verbatim and nonzero. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code: a `--filter` leg prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0, and "0 passed" is exit 0 too.
PROVE THE BLAST RADIUS: `git diff --stat` must show no control-room file and no security roster touched. Quote it. The checkout is shared — report only your own paths and never revert or stash a foreign one.
If a leg reds at a path this row does not own, attribute it with the path-attributed baseline and disclose it verbatim rather than fixing it.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (load `adversarial-self-review`). Ask, in order: after the fold, does the image build still archive the SAME bytes it did before — what would tell you if `core.autocrlf=false` changed them, given the four arms pass unedited either way? Does the shared primitive leak a temporary directory on any path where the old inline code did not, and is its teardown still prefix-fenced in BOTH callers? With the guard gone, is there any remaining caller that passes `request.workspace` and now silently has it ignored — or did you delete the key? Does the gated migrate-down arm now depend on git being present, and does it fail with a readable reason if it is not? And the question behind the row: is there anything left in the tree that still claims the migration source is the working tree?
